summary: Antioch sprawls across nearly 30 square miles at the eastern edge of Contra Costa County, where the Sacramento–San Joaquin River Delta meets the dry, golden hills that roll south toward Mount Diablo — and that geography is the defining fact of life here. The city sits far enough east that summer highs regularly push well above the 72°F annual average, baking the open grasslands amber by June, while winter mornings settle into a cool 51°F fog that burns off into reliably sunny days (nearly 9.6 hours of daylight sunshine on average). With a median home value around $607,400 against a median household income of $94,256, the price-to-income ratio lands near 6.4 — steep, but notably lower than inner Bay Area cities where the same ratio can double. The tradeoff is commute distance: Antioch is overwhelmingly a bedroom community, with eBART extending the BART system to a local station that still requires a transfer in Pittsburg/Bay Point, meaning a trip to downtown San Francisco can exceed 90 minutes door-to-door. Motor vehicle theft stands out sharply at over 1,050 per 100K, a rate well above state averages and worth weighing against the relative affordability. The Delta waterfront and nearby Contra Loma Regional Park offer genuine outdoor access — kayaking, fishing, open trails — but much of the city's interior is subdivisions connected by wide arterials rather than walkable streets. Antioch is essentially a bet that East County infrastructure will catch up to the housing that's already been built.
